To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gross domestic savings has no effect on gross domestic product but investment has.
the long run gross domestic savings and the investment multipliers are 0.55 and 0.81 respectively.
there exist a long run relationship among gross domestic savings, investments and growth and there is bidirectional causality among investment and gross domestic savings and growth in the short run.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the variables and their impact on the economic growth.
the relationship between savings, investment, and economic growth for Nepal.
the long run relationship between gross domestic savings (GDS), investment (INV) and growth (GDP) for the period of the 1974/1975 to 2010/2011 for Nepal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no direct causality relationship between gross domestic savings rate, gross domestic investment and economic growth in Nepal.
the investment and savings are complementary in Nepal.
investment is the key to economic growth and that savings is not a sufficient condition for investment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
investment has positive and significant long run effect on the economic growth in Nepal.
there is a long run equilibrium relationship between the variables.
the policy of increasing gross domestic savings and promoting investment in order to accelerate economic growth is not effective in the Nepalese context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the government of Nepal should take necessary steps in order to promote investment in the country.
the government should focus on increasing domestic savings and investment in order to accelerate growth in the long run.
investment and savings are important determinants of growth and hence, the government should take appropriate measures to increase investment and savings to accelerate the growth process.
